chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Sindi from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who comes to a group of people and claims a house that is in their possession, while the one currently holding the house presents evidence that he inherited it from his father, not knowing what the situation was regarding it. He (the Imam) said: 'If he has more evidence, he is sworn an oath and the house is returned to him.' I said: 'What if the one who claimed the house said: Indeed, this father who is in it took it without payment, and the one currently in it did not present evidence except that he inherited it from his father?' He said: 'If its situation is thus, then it belongs to the one who claimed it and presented evidence upon it.'
ai.seo_question: How is a property dispute resolved in Shia jurisprudence when both parties claim inheritance?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the evidentiary standards in property disputes, establishing that a claimant who proves the current possessor acquired the asset gratuitously (without payment) prevails over the possessor who merely claims inheritance. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the quality of proof (*bayyinah*) and the presumption of ownership (*istishab*) being overridden by clear evidence of transfer, a principle rooted in the Imams' detailed application of commercial law.
